title: Resolve specific Phytone identity and corn-starch alias ownership
body:
The worker-10 successor review found distinct plant-derived material scopes collapsed into generic owners. The inspected maintained baseline is `e000d66dd26ab053e9b17ce7bf8d3c873c3dde99`; source-specific proposals are available for Phytone and corn starch, with complete-owner publication still withheld.

A read-only GitHub `main` check at 2026-11-08T06:11:28.616136+00:00 found the relevant owner bytes identical to this frozen baseline. Exact decoded-body hashes and API captures are retained in `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-10/successor-v1/issues/current-main-owner-check.json`.

`data/ingredients/mapped/Phytone.yaml` shares the primary identifier FOODON:03315720 (hydrolyzed vegetable protein) with soy-peptone records. The source case explicitly names BBL Phytone. MicrO0001795 names Phytone peptone, and manufacturer guidance describes the papaic soybean digest while distinguishing Phytone UF and other soy products. Use the specific Phytone material identity rather than a shared generic parent, and separately reconcile Phytone aliases carried by `data/ingredients/mapped/Soy_Peptone.yaml`; do not silently merge different soy products. Primary references: [TOGO M2989](https://togomedium.org/medium/M2989), [MicrO0001795](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/micro/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FMICRO_0001795), [manufacturer technical guide](https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/BPD/brochures/peptones-supplements-feeds-technical-reference-guide.pdf). MicrO's contradictory botanical parenthetical is not evidence for barley origin and must not be copied into the ingredient.

`data/ingredients/mapped/Starch.yaml` carries an active exact `Corn Starch` alias on generic CHEBI:28017. TOGO M1812 explicitly identifies Sigma corn-origin starch, and FOODON:00005791 denotes starch powder derived from maize grain. A distinct corn-starch proposal is supported; owned-name/alias reconciliation must accompany integration so the generic owner does not continue claiming the specific name. This finding does not approve an automatic move of every rice, soluble or supplier-labelled starch alias. Primary references: [TOGO M1812](https://togomedium.org/medium/M1812), [FoodOn00005791](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/foodon/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FFOODON_00005791).

Exact proposal/evidence references are `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-10/successor-v1/bio/{decisions,evidence,proposals}.json`: cases69 and78; proposals `sv1-bio-phytone_specific_identity` and `sv1-bio-corn_starch`. The ledger binds before-owner and proposed-payload hashes.

This is a source-backed refinement of the broad withholding queue [#718](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/718). Closed [#504](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/504#issuecomment-5536067334) recorded the shared Phytone/soy identifier family and called it a benign duplicate set; the exact Phytone ontology/manufacturer evidence now supports a more specific material distinction. Closed [#114](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/114), [#170](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/170) and [#148](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/148) do not resolve these current source-specific identity/alias claims. [#1188](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/1188) addresses the different ISP4 whole-medium versus salt-parent defect.

Required follow-up: reconcile exact current owner bytes and duplicate/alias ownership, preserve source-specific products and existing rejected labels, apply only supported identity deltas through guarded writers, synchronize maintained surfaces and validate registry/SSSOM/lookup output. No product composition, species, process or whole-owner approval may be inferred from a generic hydrolysate or starch parent.
